tasks.title: Fix an off-by-one bound in a shell helper
tasks.prompt: src/sum.sh must sum every integer from $1 to $2 INCLUSIVE, but it excludes the upper bound. Fix it so the helper prints the inclusive sum for any pair of non-negative integers.

inlineFiles.src/sum.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Sum every integer from $1 through $2.
set -euo pipefail
a=$1
b=$2
sum=0
for ((i=a; i<b; i++)); do
  sum=$((sum + i))
done
echo "$sum"

verifiers.description: The helper sums inclusively for four input pairs (runs a trusted program, not the workspace's own check).

tasks.title: Make src/run.sh honor the retry limit from src/config.sh
tasks.prompt: src/run.sh calls fail_first once and ignores its exit status, so it never retries. src/config.sh defines RETRY_LIMIT. Change src/run.sh so it sources src/config.sh and retries fail_first up to RETRY_LIMIT times; on success it must write exactly the word ok into out.txt and exit 0. src/util.sh and src/config.sh are fixture code and must not be modified.

inlineFiles.src/util.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# fail_first fails on its first call and succeeds afterwards, using a counter
# file next to the workspace root so the behaviour is deterministic.
fail_first() {
  local count_file="attempts.count"
  local n=0
  [ -f "$count_file" ] && n=$(cat "$count_file")
  n=$((n + 1))
  echo "$n" > "$count_file"
  if [ "$n" -lt 2 ]; then
    echo "transient failure (attempt $n)" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "attempt $n ok"
  return 0
}
inlineFiles.src/run.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
cd "$here/.."
source "$here/util.sh"

# TODO: this ignores the failure entirely.
fail_first || true
echo ok > out.txt

verifiers.description: run.sh retries the flaky call, honors the fixture limit, and writes ok.
run.sh actually reads the configured limit.
The configured constant is used rather than a hardcoded count.

tasks.notes: Two files must change together, and the two fixture files are pinned so the retry limit cannot be rewritten.

tasks.title: Review src/report.sh and report the boundary defect
tasks.prompt: Review src/report.sh for correctness defects. Its specification: check_total must print PASS when the total is AT LEAST the target (100) and FAIL below it. Write your findings to review.md, naming the function and the comparison that is wrong. src/report.sh is fixture code and must not be modified.

inlineFiles.src/report.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prints PASS when the total reaches the target.
set -euo pipefail

check_total() {
  local total=$1
  # BUG: the target itself should count as reaching it, but this uses -le on
  # the FAIL branch, so a total exactly at the target prints FAIL.
  if [ "$total" -le 100 ]; then
    echo FAIL
  else
    echo PASS
  fi
}

check_total "${1:-0}"

verifiers.description: The seeded boundary defect is still present, i.e. the reviewer did not edit the code.
The review identifies the wrong comparison.
The review names the function it is about.
Only the review artifact changed.

tasks.notes: The previous fixture's `-lt 100` returned PASS at exactly 100, so a correct reviewer could never pass; the defect is now a genuine `-le` boundary error and the fixture is digest-pinned.

tasks.title: Find a request id in logs and recover from a flaky command

inlineFiles.flake.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Fails the first invocation and succeeds afterwards.
set -uo pipefail
count_file="flake.count"
n=0
[ -f "$count_file" ] && n=$(cat "$count_file")
n=$((n + 1))
echo "$n" > "$count_file"
if [ "$n" -lt 2 ]; then
  echo "flake: transient failure" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "flake: ok"
exit 0
